title: West Virginia's $25 cryptids sample plates are on sale online
excerpt: Display-only versions of West Virginia’s cryptids license plate sell for $25 each online. Buyers choose from nine sets of lettering, one for each creature.
content:
Display-only versions of West Virginia’s cryptids license plate sell for $25 each online. Buyers choose from nine sets of lettering, one for each creature.

Display-only versions of West Virginia’s cryptids license plate are on sale for $25 each. Orders opened at 12 a.m. Friday, November 20.

The West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles takes orders only through its online form. Buyers inside and outside the state can choose from nine sets of lettering, one for each creature on the plate.

The DMV said November 19 it had sold more than 3,000 plates for vehicles since the November 2 launch.

“We knew West Virginians loved their cryptids, but this response has been incredible,” Governor Patrick Morrisey said in a release from the West Virginia Department of Transportation.

Drivers who want the road plate can get it at a West Virginia DMV office or call the agency’s in-state toll-free line at 800-642-9066. Those plates carry the letters ET followed by numbers.

Drivers pay a $10 scenic plate fee on top of the regular $51.50 registration renewal fee. For drivers exchanging a plate with time left on its registration, the DMV prorates the renewal fee and charges a $10 exchange fee. The DMV says it will keep the plate in its scenic lineup as long as there’s demand.

Former DMV Commissioner Steven O. Dale said in the release that the plate is the latest product of a 60-year partnership between the DMV, the Division of Corrections and 3M. Dale works with the company that applies the graphics before the Division of Corrections stamps the numbers.

Both versions use the same artwork by Jesse Corlis, a muralist whose work can be found in West Virginia and other states. Corlis created the cryptids design while working for the DMV and also designed the Protect Pollinators plate featuring a bee and the wildlife plate featuring a turtle. He died in 2023, before the cryptids plate went on sale.

“First and foremost, I would like to pay tribute to Jesse Corlis, the talented graphic artist who designed the Cryptid license plate,” DMV Commissioner Everett Frazier said in the release.

Corlis set the nine creatures in a West Virginia forest. The design includes Braxton County’s Flatwoods Monster, also called Braxie, as well as Mothman from Kanawha and Mason counties, Batboy from Greenbrier County and the Grafton Monster from Taylor County.

Marion County accounts for two creatures, Veggie Man and Ogua. The plate also features the Webster County Werewolf, Sheepsquatch from an area stretching from Boone County to Mason County and Bigfoot, which the DMV said has been reported across the country, including in many West Virginia counties.
